stem: A unit's fall rate has increased for three consecutive months. Which action by the staff nurse best reflects the RN's role in performance improvement?

options.A: Wait for senior administration to solve the problem because entry-level RNs do not participate in quality-improvement work involving client outcomes.
options.B: Change the fall-prevention policy independently and immediately because an individual nurse should bypass the unit's improvement process when outcome data worsen.
options.C: Participate in the structured improvement process by reviewing the data and evidence, helping test appropriate changes, and evaluating their effect on client outcomes.
options.D: Stop reporting falls until a new prevention strategy is selected because reducing the number of incident reports will make the unit's performance data more accurate.

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan includes participation in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes, use of research and references, and evaluation of the impact of improvement measures on client care and resource use. C therefore best reflects the staff RN's role. A wrongly excludes entry-level nurses, B bypasses the organized improvement/policy process, and D corrupts safety data rather than improving outcomes.
educational_objective: Participate appropriately in structured performance-improvement work by using data/evidence, testing changes through the process, and evaluating outcomes.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: participate in PI/QI processes, utilize research/references, evaluate impact on client care/resource use.
source_claim_supported: Entry-level RNs participate in structured quality-improvement processes and evaluate improvement effects on client outcomes.
